title: The opt-in snapshot of the erase count sits outside the pure ReminderMode transition
evidence: ReminderScheduler.optIn() (ReminderScheduler.swift:104) runs `if case .off = mode { seenErasures = erasures() }` before it sends tappedOn: a tap made while off takes a fresh erase count, so the next refresh does not end an opt-in made after an erase. The rule lives in the scheduler, not in the pure ReminderMode transition, so the ReminderModeTests table cannot see it. Only two scheduler tests guard it: ReminderSchedulerTests.swift:346 (testAnOptInBeforeTheRefreshThatSeesTheEraseHolds_US25_AC12b) and :360 (testAllowNotificationsAfterAnUnseenHeldEraseStillEndsReminders_US25_AC12b). Fix: move the snapshot into the transition (tappedOn from off names a resnapshot effect) and add rows to the ReminderModeTests table.
